events.title: TRS-80 Model I released
events.summary: Radio Shack began selling the TRS-80 Model I in August 1977 — bringing personal computing to its nationwide retail chain.
events.about: The 'Trash-80' ran Level I BASIC on a Z80 with cassette storage and optional floppy drives. Radio Shack's store footprint put PCs in suburban malls — not just computer fairs. Developers wrote business software, games, and magazine type-in programs; the platform trained hobbyists who later moved to IBM compatibles.

narrative.whyChosen: The TRS-80 was the first mass-retail personal computer sold through a national electronics chain.
narrative.whyImportant: It proved consumer electronics stores could move complete computer systems at scale.
narrative.problemSolved: Personal computers were sold through niche mail-order and hobby shops with little mainstream reach.
